content.text: an option for P. falciparum only in Haiti, Dominican Republic, Central America west and north of the Panama Canal and parts of the Middle East; resistance is widespread elsewhere; P. vivax where there is no chloroquine resistance: a 3-drug regimen of chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine, primaquine and tafenoquine; primaquine or tafenoquine needs G6PD screening first (hemolytic anemia); pregnancy: chloroquine can be used where Plasmodium is susceptible.

adult dose (uncomplicated, chloroquine-sensitive): 1 g salt (600 mg base), then 500 mg (300 mg base) after six to eight h, then 500 mg (300 mg base) on each of two consecutive days. CI (uses other than acute malaria): retinal or visual field changes of any cause. QT prolongation, torsades and ventricular arrhythmias reported (greater risk at high doses); caution in cardiac dz, ventricular arrhythmia hx, uncorrected low K and/or Mg, brady (< 50 bpm) or w QT-prolonging drugs. Can cause severe, life-threatening hypoglycemia, w or w.o antidiabetic meds; antidiabetic drug doses may need ↓. Irreversible retinal damage; risk factors: > 2.3 mg/kg/day (actual body wt), use > five yrs, subnormal GFR, drugs such as tamoxifen; stop if ocular toxicity is suspected (changes may progress after stopping). Fatal accidental ingestions in children (0.75 or 1 g in one 3-year-old): keep out of children's reach. May precipitate a severe psoriasis attack (⍉ in psoriasis unless benefit outweighs risk); may exacerbate porphyria (⍉ in porphyria); hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.
